Long-run effects from a common correlated effects fit

Source: R/lrc.R
lrcce.Rd

The cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) long-run effects of Chudik et al. (2016) as Ditzen (2021, sec. 3.2) sets them out, from the unit estimates of ccepnl().

Usage

lrcce(object, x, ylag = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

An object of class ccepnl, or a data frame or matrix of unit estimates with one named column per term (as its bi).

x

The terms of one regressor and its lags (columns of bi), or a named list of such sets, one long-run effect each.

ylag

NULL (the columns named L1.y, L2.y, ... of bi) or the names of the columns holding the lags of y.

level

The confidence level of the intervals.

Value

A data frame, one row per long-run effect and a last row "phi": term, est (the mean group estimate), se, z, p, lo, hi; with the unit values as the attribute units (a matrix, units by rows of the table).

Details

A dynamic panel y_it = mu_i + sum_l lambda_l,i y_i,t-l + sum_l beta_l,i x_i,t-l + averages + e_it fitted unit by unit (ccepnl() with ylag lags of y and the lags of x as columns of its x) has the long-run effect of x on the steady state of y theta_i = sum_l beta_l,i / (1 - sum_l lambda_l,i) (Ditzen 2021, eq. 3 and sec. 3.2). Each unit's theta_i is computed from its estimates; the mean group estimate is their mean and its variance the mean group variance sum_i (theta_i - mean)^2 / (N (N - 1)) (Pesaran and Smith 1995, as Chudik et al. 2016 apply it). The adjustment speed phi_i = 1 - sum_l lambda_l,i of the error-correction form (Ditzen 2021, sec. 3.1) is reported the same way as "phi".

The cross-sectionally augmented distributed lag (CS-DL) estimator of the same paper needs no function of its own: ccepnl() with x and its first differences x_t - x_t-1, ..., lagged up to floor(T^(1/3)) - 1, as regressors and ylag = 0 estimates theta as the coefficient of x (Ditzen 2021, sec. 3.3); see the examples. Ditzen (2021, sec. 3.3) also lags the averages of x up to floor(T^(1/3)) and keeps the average of y unlagged, where ccepnl(lags = ) lags both.

The exponent of cross-sectional dependence of Bailey, Kapetanios and Pesaran (2016), the other topic of Ditzen (2021), is not built here (its bias correction is not set out in Ditzen 2021); Pesaran's CD test is pcdtst().

References

Ditzen, J. (2021). Estimating long-run effects and the exponent of cross-sectional dependence: an update to xtdcce2. The Stata Journal, 21(3), 687-707. doi:10.1177/1536867X211045560

Chudik, A., Mohaddes, K., Pesaran, M. H. and Raissi, M. (2016). Long-run effects in large heterogeneous panel data models with cross-sectionally correlated errors. In Essays in Honor of Aman Ullah (Advances in Econometrics, vol. 36), 85-135. Emerald.

Pesaran, M. H. and Smith, R. (1995). Estimating long-run relationships from dynamic heterogeneous panels. Journal of Econometrics, 68, 79-113. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(94)01644-F

Bailey, N., Kapetanios, G. and Pesaran, M. H. (2016). Exponent of cross-sectional dependence: estimation and inference. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 31, 929-960. doi:10.1002/jae.2476

Examples

set.seed(3)
tt <- 30
d <- expand.grid(year = 1:tt, prov = paste0("p", 1:25))
f <- rnorm(tt)[d$year]
g <- rnorm(25, 1)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))]
d$x <- g * f + rnorm(nrow(d))
d$xl <- ave(d$x, d$prov, FUN = function(v) c(NA, v[-length(v)]))
d$y <- 0
for (i in which(d$year > 1)) {
  d$y[i] <- 0.4 * d$y[i - 1] + 0.5 * d$x[i] + 0.1 * d$xl[i] +
    g[i] * f[i] + rnorm(1)
}
k <- d$year > 1
# CS-ARDL: theta is 0.6 over 0.6, that is 1
r <- ccepnl(d$y[k], d[k, c("x", "xl")], d$prov[k], d$year[k], ylag = 1)
lrcce(r, c("x", "xl"))
#>   term       est         se         z            p        lo        hi
#> 1    x 1.2095957 0.26532667  4.558892 5.142412e-06 0.6895650 1.7296265
#> 2  phi 0.6980514 0.05501332 12.688771 6.824871e-37 0.5902273 0.8058755
# CS-DL: x and its first difference; the coefficient of x is theta
d$dx <- d$x - d$xl
ccepnl(d$y[k], d[k, c("x", "dx")], d$prov[k], d$year[k], lags = 3)$mg
#>   term        est         se         z            p         lo         hi
#> 1    x  0.8218133 0.10435066  7.875497 3.393915e-15  0.6172897  1.0263368
#> 2   dx -0.2750372 0.06408953 -4.291453 1.775074e-05 -0.4006504 -0.1494241
